finding.summary: Caller-supplied prewoken_goal_ids are accepted as wake lineage without binding them to a wake_due transition or an equivalent wake receipt. Any non-empty supplied iterable also bypasses the due_for_tick guard.
observed_logic: prewoken_goal_ids plus observed_events is rejected as ambiguous
otherwise prewoken_goal_ids are converted directly to strings and assigned to woken
due_for_tick is checked only when woken is empty
the supplied values are subsequently persisted in the cognitive-cycle checkpoint and COGNITIVE_CYCLE_COMMITTED event
finding.risk: A buggy or untrusted wrapper can force an early heartbeat/cognitive cycle and persist false wake lineage without a matching deferred-intent wake transition. This does not grant EffectGate authority, but it weakens deterministic scheduler causality and receipt provenance.
finding.counterhypothesis: The API may be intended only for a trusted in-process scheduler wrapper. Even under that interpretation, the trust/binding invariant is implicit rather than enforced at the shared runtime boundary, so accidental misuse remains fail-open.
finding.recommended_fix: Replace naked prewoken goal IDs with a verifiable wake receipt/token bound to the same agency state transition, or at minimum validate supplied goal IDs against exact current post-wake state plus an event identity tied to the cycle. Do not let mere non-empty caller input bypass schedule due-ness.
finding.cheapest_discriminator: Set next_tick_not_before in the future, call tick_once with no observed_events and a fabricated non-empty prewoken_goal_ids value, and assert that the runtime rejects it without heartbeat/cognitive-cycle credit. The exact-current source is predicted to fail this acceptance test.
